input.quote: (d) Termination for Competing Product of Sanofi. If after [***]: (i) Sanofi or its Affiliates, alone or with or through a Third Party, develop, manufacture or commercialize a Competing Product and (ii) Sanofi or its Affiliates have not commenced a Registrational Clinical Trial for a Product prior to commencing the activities in Section 12.2(d)(i), RevMed may terminate this Agreement effective [***] after it delivers written notice to Sanofi that it is exercising its rights under this Section 12.2(d) unless Sanofi elects in writing within such [***] period to [***].
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use covenant binding Sanofi, which meets the preferred position. Searches for "compete", "shall not develop", "Sanofi shall not / will not" and "Exclusivity" return no restrictive covenant on Sanofi; the only covenants running against Sanofi are the mutual debarment/compliance/pharmacovigilance covenants in Section 13.4, and Section 13.3 covenants bind RevMed only. The licensed "Field" is defined as "any and all uses" (p0053), so there is no field limitation on our business, and Section 3.8 expressly provides that neither Party must "agree to any restrictions on the businesses of RevMed or Sanofi or its Affiliates" to obtain clearance (p0271). The functional restraint the planner flagged, Section 12.2(d), is not a prohibition: Sanofi remains free to develop, manufacture or commercialize a Competing Product, and the sole consequence is a RevMed termination right that (i) arises only after a stated period, (ii) is unavailable once Sanofi has commenced a Registrational Clinical Trial for a Product, (iii) operates during the Term only with no post-term restraint, and (iv) can be defeated by a Sanofi written election. The resulting reversion/transition consequences in Section 12.3(c) are the same package that applies to Sanofi's own termination for convenience, so they are not an incremental competitive restraint. The Section 15.2 Acquiror-Family separation conditions in (A)-(D) attach to the RevMed-as-acquired-Party case (p0613/p0614); for Sanofi, p0612 excludes acquirer IP and the Acquiror Family unconditionally, which favours us. Two sub-elements fall short of an ideal draft and are noted rather than flagged: the "Competing Product" definition (p0037) is redacted, so its breadth cannot be fully verified, and there is no express carve-out for internal development or acquisitions in Section 12.2(d) — but as 12.2(d) creates only a termination right rather than a covenant, this does not restrict our business and no redline is warranted.
